plan.title: Mouse tumor immune/stromal composition: anti-PD-1 vs isotype
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 mouse subcutaneous tumor samples (6 anti-PD-1 treated vs 6 isotype control, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes) are profiled for sample structure and library depth, since sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. mMCP-counter is the mouse-specific tool of record for immune/stromal cell composition from bulk gene expression (marker-based, quantifies 16 populations, validated by flow cytometry per Petitprez et al. 2020, Genome Medicine) — human deconvolution tools (MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTiseq) are explicitly forbidden on mouse data per the knowledge service, since their marker/reference profiles are human-derived and not transferable. UCell rank-based scoring of PanglaoDB mouse immune/stromal marker genes is run as a descriptive complement (not a deconvolution), giving a second, orthogonal view of composition that does not depend on the mMCP-counter marker panel. Composition estimates from both methods are statistically compared between anti-PD-1 and isotype control groups (Wilcoxon rank-sum per cell type/signature with BH correction across cell types/signatures), and reported beside — not substituting for — a DESeq2 differential expression analysis of the same contrast, since a treatment-driven composition shift is itself a form of and confound for the DE signal. All steps ground in the actual dataset: 12 samples, 6 vs 6, mouse gene symbols, tissue = subcutaneous tumor.
